title: Function-Preserving Audits of Visual Weight Readers

target_networks.name: Shallow ReLU neural fields (six shape classes, MNIST digits)
SIREN neural fields of CIFAR10 images (2-64-64-3; released 2-32-32-3)

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 3 reader seeds per method (official audit); 5-6 seeds in feature-location studies; 3 fresh responses per side per origin for LLM readers

key_claims.claim: High accuracy on original weights can coexist with strong sensitivity to function-preserving reparameterizations; a shape statistics reader falls from 96.7% to 24.2% under joint permutation and rescaling.
key_claims.quote: Shape Stats ridge falls from 96.7% to 24.2% under joint permutation and rescaling: 87 of 120 correct predictions become incorrect and none improve.

key_claims.claim: Matched controls localise the failure: phase wrapping removes phase dependence and sign-invariant Gram features also remove sign dependence.
key_claims.quote: Phase wrapping removes phase sensitivity; Gram features also remove sign sensitivity.

key_claims.claim: Invariance is not enough: complete canonical hidden features reach 38.7% on MNIST while explicitly composing them into field outputs reaches 81.5%.

key_claims.quote: Qwen2.5-0.5B gives the same letter on all 60 original and redacted inputs. A Qwen3.5-27B control reads 7/60 weight inputs but 60/60 explicit cues.

limitations_stated.text: Scope is limited to shallow ReLU and two-hidden-layer SIREN fields, with one released configuration per method.

limitations_stated.text: Generated-answer tests assume independent stationary calls and have limited power at three repeats per side.

notes_for_review: Not a weight-editing study: it audits readers of neural-field weights (learned metanetworks and, in a side study, GPT-6 family LLMs reading six-digit weights of tiny ReLU shape fields) with function-preserving transformations. Its relevance to WSP is methodological: an LLM 'reading' weights should be tested with symmetry-equivalent inputs and with repeats on both inputs, since repeat disagreement alone is 13-17% for Astra and Sol. The LLM study is small (60 origins, 720 prospective responses) and the visual tasks are toy-scale; Codex assisted much of the work, as the authors state.
